title: Sony's decision to ditch discs was practically inevitable, data shows
gist: Circana data cited by analyst Mat Piscatella shows US physical game sales collapsed from a 2009 peak of 297 million units ($11.5B) to just 37 million units ($1.6B) over the last 12 months, with PlayStation losing far more ground than Nintendo, explaining why Sony's 2028 disc discontinuation is more a lagging acknowledgment than a bold bet.

themes.theme: Secular collapse in physical game sales

insights.claim: US physical video game unit sales peaked at 297 million in the 12 months ending June 2009 and have declined steadily since, to just 37 million units in the most recent 12-month period.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: An 87%+ collapse in physical unit sales from peak quantifies exactly how far the disc-based distribution model has eroded, directly supporting the rationale for Sony's move away from discs.
insights.locator: Circana data graph description, early paragraphs

insights.claim: Physical video game spending in the US fell from a peak of $11.5 billion in 2009 to just $1.6 billion for the 12 months ending in May.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: An 86% dollar-spend decline over 16 years shows physical retail's economic relevance to publishers/platform holders has become marginal, informing the terminal value of physical game retail as an asset class.

insights.claim: Only seven PlayStation games sold over 100,000 physical units in the US in 2026 so far, versus 100 PlayStation games hitting that threshold in 2008.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: A roughly 93% collapse in the number of PlayStation titles reaching a meaningful physical sales bar is a specific, platform-level confirmation of the broader disc decline.
insights.locator: 'only seven PlayStation games had sold over 100,000 physical units' paragraph

insights.claim: The best-selling physical PlayStation game of 2026 so far has sold only about 275,000 units in the US.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Even the ceiling for physical PlayStation sales has become modest, indicating disc revenue is no longer material even for hit titles on Sony's platform.
insights.locator: 'the top-selling physical PlayStation game has only sold' sentence

insights.claim: Aggregate US physical video game spending was actually up 4 percent year-to-date versus the prior year, but Piscatella attributed essentially all of that growth to Nintendo Switch 2 physical sales, while PlayStation and other platforms saw physical spending drops in the teens to mid-30s percent range.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Nintendo's continued cartridge/physical strength versus Sony's near-total digital shift shows the disc decline is platform-strategy-dependent, not a uniform industry death — relevant for differentiating Nintendo's physical-media economics from Sony's/Xbox's.
insights.quote: the Switch 2 and physical sales growth on Nintendo platforms
insights.locator: quoting Piscatella on the 4% YTD increase

insights.claim: 27 percent of all PS5 hardware sold in the US has been the 'Digital Only' edition, versus 52 percent of all Xbox Series hardware sold.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Xbox's digital-only hardware mix is nearly double PlayStation's, indicating Xbox's console economics are already further down the disc-elimination path than Sony's — a useful comparator for modeling platform-holder margin trajectories.
insights.locator: '27 percent of all PS5 hardware' sentence

insights.claim: Console gamers' willingness to pay for digital downloads was already evident by the late 2000s through services like Xbox Live Arcade, PSN, and WiiWare, which expanded into full downloadable versions of major releases like Infamous and LittleBigPlanet.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: The digital shift's roots trace back nearly two decades, meaning Sony's 2028 disc cutoff is the tail end of a long, well-telegraphed trend rather than a sudden strategic pivot.

insights.claim: By the time the PlayStation Vita launched in 2012, Sony began requiring publishers making physical game cartridges to also offer a downloadable option, a policy that later consoles like the Wii U, PS4, and Xbox One continued, making disc-exclusive releases nearly extinct by the end of the 2010s.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Sony itself institutionalized the digital-parity requirement over a decade ago, showing the platform holder has been steering toward this outcome deliberately, not just reacting to it now.
insights.locator: 'By the time the PlayStation Vita launched in 2012' paragraph

insights.claim: Some big-budget titles now skip retail entirely or use hybrid 'download in a box' options such as Switch 2's Game Key Cards or Grand Theft Auto VI's printed download codes.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Hybrid physical/digital packaging is becoming the norm even for retail-channel releases, a transitional retail format worth tracking as discs phase out entirely.
insights.locator: 'In recent years, some big-budget games' sentence

insights.claim: Given the data, Sony does not appear worried about losing what is, financially, a now-small segment of its gaming business by discontinuing discs.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: The article's core thesis — that the disc phase-out is low-risk for Sony given how immaterial physical revenue has become — frames the move as a rational cost-cutting/simplification step rather than a customer-alienating gamble.
